minutes.headline: Committee re-elected its officers by roll call and divided tasks for the September 26 town meet and greet.
minutes.summary: The Economic Development Committee approved the June minutes and reorganized, with officers chosen by one roll-call vote. It then discussed how to join a planning board meeting without a quorum. Most of the meeting was a task-by-task plan for the second annual meet and greet, including donations, supplies and volunteers.

budget_items.topic: Meet and greet monetary donation goal
budget_items.what_was_said: A monetary goal was set for sponsorships because last year's donations were small and members paid out of pocket. Donations come by email or Venmo with the Town of Lunenburg noted.

budget_items.topic: Planning office budget for printing and supplies
budget_items.what_was_said: Members recalled that the planning office budget is itemized and could cover flyers, banners and name tags but not an event line. They discussed asking the planning board to add the event to its annual budget.

budget_items.topic: Town covering the full event cost
budget_items.what_was_said: A member doubted the town could be asked to cover the whole amount but thought it could help with specific items.
The needs list includes food, disposables and promotional displays, and a member paid personally for a DJ and a portable toilet last year.
A member was asked for accurate costs of the DJ and porta-potty she had already paid so they can be built into the budget.
Catering from Market Basket cost about this much last year and is expected to be more this year with higher attendance.

decisions.decision: Aim to join the planning board's August meeting; Kathy will ask the planning staff about availability on the biweekly Mondays (dates as heard: the 5th and 18th).
Best practice agreed: post a meeting when a quorum may attend the planning board session; if no quorum, members attend as individuals and speak only as members.
Ask the planning board at the joint meeting to add the meet and greet as a standing item in its annual budget.
Meet and greet tasks were assigned to named members: restaurant sponsorships, beverages, tents and tables, flyers, a sponsorship letter, logos and outreach.
After the meet and greet, the committee will reconvene to choose its next focus, and may invite economic development staff from neighboring towns.

what_happened.line: The committee chose its officers (chair, vice chair, clerk) in a single motion that passed 4-0 by roll call.
Members agreed on a practice for joining a planning board meeting: post a meeting if a quorum may attend, otherwise attend as individuals.
The committee aims to join the planning board's August meeting; one member will ask planning staff about availability.
Members agreed to ask the planning board to add the second annual meet and greet as a standing item in its annual budget.
Meet and greet tasks (sponsorships, beverages, tents, flyers, outreach) were assigned to named members.

why_it_matters: The meet and greet was funded last year by donations and by members paying out of pocket, so a request to put it in the planning board's budget would be a recurring town line item residents could be asked to support.
The committee has no budget of its own for the event, and the planning office's itemized budget may cover printing and supplies but not an event line.
watch_next: The joint meeting with the planning board in August, where the committee plans to ask for the meet and greet to become a standing budget item.
The September 26 meet and greet, after which the committee will choose its next focus.
